article_text: The upcoming visit of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to Japan presents a significant opportunity to strengthen Bangladesh's economic potential and international partnerships. According to government statements, the primary focus of this visit, scheduled for 26 October, is bilateral relations, economic partnerships, and investment. To transform these expectations into sustainable achievements, clear preparation and consistent implementation are necessary. The foundation of this relationship was established during the post-independence reconstruction period. On 10 February 1972, Japan recognised Bangladesh, and diplomatic relations were established. Since then, the continuity of relationships and cooperation has been maintained during various governments. This five-decade trust is a valuable diplomatic asset for Bangladesh. Collaboration on projects like the Jamuna Multipurpose Bridge, Japanese financing, and technical involvement in Dhaka's metro rail and Jamuna railway bridge have significantly contributed to the communication system. The Bay of Bengal Industrial Growth Belt (BIG-B) initiative in 2014 unveiled the integrated potential of infrastructure, industry, and regional connectivity. Matarbari and Araihazar are the foundations for expanding that cooperation. Evaluating the achievements of existing projects and the potential of ongoing initiatives can enhance production, employment, and local businesses. Prime Minister to visit Japan tomorrow, raising hopes for fresh investment momentum The first priority could be preparing to leverage the benefits of the Economic Partnership Agreement (EPA) signed on 6 February 2026. Joint action plans on essential processes for implementing the agreement, tariff regulations, rules of origin, certification, and customs procedures are required. Guidelines for small and medium exporters and training for officials will be helpful. Besides garments, market research can be conducted on leather goods, processed food, and light engineering sectors. To transform market advantages into sustainable trade, standards, punctuality, and consistent supply are essential. In investment discussions, specific proposals, including prepared land, electricity, water, transport connections, and approval systems, could be fruitful. Based on the Araihazar Economic Zone, feasibility studies on machinery, electrical equipment, packaging, and food processing can be conducted. Encouraging joint ventures among Japanese medium-sized enterprises and Bangladeshi entrepreneurs, considering local suppliers, skilled workers, and market demand, is essential alongside large corporations. Administrative reliability will support these efforts. A system for resolving investors' issues within a specified timeframe can increase predictability in approvals, tariff applications, and financial transactions. If the benefits of similar reforms reach domestic businesses as well, the overall investment environment will improve. Ambassador to stay away from Tokyo during PM's Japan visit, ministry secretary sent to coordinate In infrastructure cooperation, connecting the development of Matarbari Port and the Maheshkhali-Matarbari area with roads, railways, warehouses, customs, and industrial zones is crucial. Joint initiatives to reduce the time and cost of goods transportation through digital customs, risk-based inspections, operational training, and information exchange can be undertaken. Considering loan terms, foreign currency repayment obligations, usage, and maintenance expenses in new projects will enhance the economic sustainability of cooperation. In human resource collaboration, the 2019 framework on skilled workers needs to be more effectively linked with the practical needs of employers. Joint curricula could emphasise language and technical training, comprehensible employment contracts, cost transparency, prevention of unscrupulous mediation, and grievance resolution. With an increase in worker numbers, equal importance must be given to improving skills, income, and protection. The long-term goal should be to enrich the country's production and knowledge base alongside overseas employment. Training in Japanese institutions, joint factories in Bangladesh, and opportunities for returning workers to become entrepreneurs can be integrated into a single plan. The recognition of qualifications, research environment, and investment facilities will encourage voluntary return and the dissemination of skills within the country. This will extend the benefits of migration beyond remittances. Bangladesh's industrial history provides significant examples in this context. In the late 1970s, the country's garment sector spread production and management knowledge across the clothing industry with the assistance of trained workers and South Korea's Daewoo. This experience shows that the enduring achievements of international cooperation lie in the learning capabilities of people and institutions. In the current partnership, it is essential to consider what skills remain in the country after a project's completion. Collaboration with Japanese partners on joint research and practical training with universities, polytechnics, and industrial enterprises will be beneficial in this regard. Cooperation can be increased in machinery maintenance, quality control, water management, and disaster-resilient construction. Alongside technology acquisition, capabilities in management, repair, and adaptation to local needs must be developed. PM's Japan visit to prioritise economic partnership, investment: Humaiun In environment and energy sectors, the cooperation memorandum of February 2026 can be utilised to assess opportunities for energy savings, waste management, rooftop solar power, and disaster preparedness in industries. Considering local capability and long-term operational costs, choosing initiatives will reduce production costs and environmental risks. These Japan-focused initiatives need to be part of Bangladesh's integrated East Asia strategy. The production and supply network of China, Japan's industrial technology, and quality management, combined with South Korea's production and technology experience, can be coordinated with Bangladesh's priorities. Bangladesh's strategic position of development-centric autonomy can be useful. Recognising the unique value of each relationship, mutual trust, national interests, and freedom of decision-making must be maintained. Closer cooperation with Japan and close ties with China can create complementary developmental opportunities. Common standards in loan sustainability, transparent procurement processes, information security, environment, and effective state control over critical infrastructure will make this position credible. Utilising its location in the Bay of Bengal, Bangladesh can be an effective connector between the markets of South Asia and the production systems of East Asia. For this, along with integrated transportation and customs, mutually agreed trade systems with neighbours are necessary. If local production, repair services, research, and suppliers are developed, the benefits of the connection will remain within the country. Diversity in financing, technology, and import sources will also increase economic resilience. In a five to ten-year East Asia cooperation plan, priority industries, supplier capabilities, training, joint research, and production stages can be determined. Opportunities for local procurement and learning on mutually agreeable terms need to be increased. Indicators of evaluation will be realistic investment, domestic value addition, worker income, local orders, and technical capabilities. There are opportunities to expand cooperation in maritime security, disaster assistance, international law, and peaceful dispute resolution. Japan's consistent diplomatic involvement is expected in creating a conducive environment for humanitarian aid for the Rohingya and for safe, voluntary, and dignified repatriation. After the visit, publishing an implementation list with responsible agencies, timelines, and a review process will be helpful. In the six-month and one-year progress assessments, announced investments, actual cash flow and production, and training and employment need to be considered separately. title: Court-declared mayor Shahadat now appointed Chattogram City administrator
description: Bangladesh’s government has appointed BNP leader Shahadat Hossain, who became Chattogram mayor after a court ruling, as administrator of Chattogram City Corporation on a full-time basis. The Local Government Division issued the order, effective immediately and until further notice, amid questions over the elected council’s expired five-year term and Hossain’s continued mayoral tenure. A similar March proposal had not been ordered. Hossain became mayor after an election tribunal overturned the 2021 result; he was sworn in during November.
article_text: The government has appointed ruling Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) leader Shahadat Hossain, who became mayor of Chattogram City Corporation following a court ruling, as the administrator of the same corporation. He was appointed on a full-time basis through a notification issued by the Local Government Division on Sunday (25 October). The Local Government Division had prepared a proposal to appoint Shahadat Hossain as administrator in March as well, but no order was issued at the time. He has now been appointed administrator amid questions over the tenure of the elected council and his continuation in the mayoral office. The notification, signed by Local Government Division Deputy Secretary Jewel Rana, states that Shahadat Hossain will serve as administrator until further orders under Section 4 of the Local Government (City Corporation) (Amendment) Act, 2026. According to the notification, he will receive monthly remuneration and other allowances in accordance with the rules. The order, issued in the public interest, takes immediate effect. Questions over tenure; previous move to appoint him administrator On 27 April, Prothom Alo ran a report on the tenure of Chattogram City Corporation’s elected council and Shahadat Hossain’s continuation in office. Citing documents from the Local Government Division, the report said the elected council held its first meeting on 23 February 2021. Accordingly, its five-year term ended on 22 February this year. Shahadat Hossain, however, had told Prothom Alo at the time that, under a court order, his tenure would continue until November 2029. However, documents from the Local Government Division stated that although the court had declared him mayor, it had issued no separate direction regarding the length of his tenure. According to the report, a proposal to appoint Shahadat as a full-time administrator had been prepared in March, but no order was issued. Earlier, on 3 February, the Local Government Division had written to the election commission requesting that arrangements be made to hold an election. BNP leader Shahadat Hossain contested the mayoral election of Chattogram City Corporation held on 27 January 2021. According to the results announced at the time, Awami League candidate Rezaul Karim Chowdhury was declared the winner with 369,248 votes. Shahadat Hossain, his closest rival, was shown to have received 52,489 votes. Alleging widespread irregularities and vote-rigging, Shahadat filed a case with the election tribunal on 24 February that year, seeking to have the results annulled. Nine people, including the then chief election commissioner, were named as defendants. Following the fall of the Awami League government on 5 August 2024, Rezaul Karim Chowdhury was removed from the mayoral post. On 19 August that year, the government appointed Chattogram Divisional Commissioner Md Tofail Islam as administrator of the city corporation. Subsequently, on 1 October, Mohammad Khairul Amin, judge of the Chattogram election tribunal and joint district and sessions judge, delivered a verdict in Shahadat’s case. The ruling overturned the decision to declare Rezaul Karim Chowdhury elected and declared Shahadat Hossain the elected mayor. It also directed that a notification be issued to this effect within 10 days. Following the court’s order, the election commission issued a revised notification on 8 October, declaring Shahadat Hossain mayor. He was sworn in on 3 November in the conference room of the Local Government Division at the Secretariat. AF Hassan Ariff, the then local government adviser to the interim government, administered the oath. Nearly three years and nine months after the election, Shahadat was sworn in as mayor. He will now run the corporation as an administrator appointed by the government.
